prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system must support continuous compliant potable-water production, utility targets/customer demand, timely operator visibility, dependable automatic control, and manual intervention.

Boundary: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood) and Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment/disinfection/storage to High Service Pump Header; excludes entire distribution network. River Intake Pump Station maintains raw-water availability within approved withdrawal limits; normally automatic, starts governed by demand/channel depth; reduced-capacity service applies for river-level, equipment, or downstream-demand constraints. Raw Water Screen Channel monitors upstream/downstream/differential levels, rake run status, and high-debris indications.

Storm Intake Mode requires closer supervision for rainfall, river rise, debris, or upstream runoff. Chief Operator authorizes entry when observations/trends invalidate normal assumptions; staff increase river-level, screen-loading, turbidity, and pump-cycling observation.

Coagulant Dosing Skid controls chemical feed using approved setpoints, raw-water conditions, and operator direction. Parallel North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery provide equipment status, headloss/turbidity monitoring, and backwash control. Chlorine Contact Basin manages disinfection contact; Clearwell Level Controller coordinates finished-water storage. Backwash Recovery Tank supports recovery.

SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) stores operating data for trends, compliance, incident reconstruction, and evaluation. Controllers, panels, workstations, analytical instruments, and historian must share plant time standards.

Chemical Supplier Driver follows controlled delivery procedures; inventory changes are checked before affecting setpoints. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench receives process/compliance samples. Laboratory Technician confirms analyses, sends unusual results to operations, and assesses adjustment verification. Chief Operator controls modes, production targets, treatment/abnormal response. Duty Engineer controls configuration, evaluates problems, approves engineering changes. Maintenance Planner converts equipment-condition information into coordinated work. Distribution Dispatcher communicates demand/delivery expectations; North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station influence pumping. Residuals Hauler interfaces residuals/backwash removal. External interfaces include electric power service and chemical/laboratory/distribution coordination.

Chlorine Residual Alarm requires immediate operator assessment. Trained staff supervise automation, implement safe manual operation, and document deviations through approved procedures.

New part:
S033: A rising differential level across the Raw Water Screen Channel is treated as an early indication of screen blinding or heavy floating debris.
S034: The Raw Water Screen Channel sends the Rake Torque Snapshot at the end of each cleaning cycle to preserve the recorded loading condition.
S035: If the Raw Water Screen Channel shows rapid level change, plant staff verify that the cleaning mechanism is running and that the River Intake Pump Station is not drawing the channel down too quickly.
S036: A high-high level condition at the Raw Water Screen Channel requires immediate field confirmation because it may indicate restricted passage, failed cleaning, or abnormal river backwater.
S037: Raw-water quality triggers include high turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints from field staff, visible sheen, algae accumulation, and rapid temperature change.
S038: When a raw-water quality trigger occurs, the Chief Operator determines whether to adjust pumping rate, request additional laboratory testing, or increase downstream process monitoring.
S039: The Laboratory Technician supports intake decisions by prioritizing raw-water checks when storm runoff or an abnormal visual condition is reported.
S040: The Coagulant Dosing Skid is placed under closer observation when intake turbidity changes faster than the normal control response can stabilize.
S041: The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are advised when incoming water quality is expected to shorten filter run time or increase solids loading.
S042: Pump permissives at the River Intake Pump Station include adequate suction level, available discharge path, healthy motor status, open isolation valves, and absence of active protective trips.
S043: A pump is not permitted to start when the Raw Water Screen Channel downstream level is below the established low-level limit.
S044: A pump start is also blocked when the associated drive reports a fault, when local control is selected, or when a safety interlock is not proven.
S045: If a permissive is lost during operation, the control system either alarms the condition or stops the affected pump according to the severity of the signal.
S046: The Chief Operator may authorize temporary manual operation only when the cause is understood, the equipment can be observed, and the risk to treatment continuity is acceptable.
S047: The SCADA Historian Server retains river level, screen differential, pump status, and raw-water quality trends for operating review and event reconstruction.
S048: The Duty Engineer reviews storm forecasts and river-stage information when a prolonged debris event or high-flow period is expected.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
